technical-seo.html.a: Technical SEO refers to all the elements on your site code and infrastructure that can help search engines crawl, render, index and understand your site. A technical SEO audit will show you any crawl errors, index coverage, speed, structured data, canonical tags and site architecture issues to help you identify what is stopping you from increasing your organic visibility.

technical-seo.html.q: How do Core Web Vitals impact rankings?
technical-seo.html.a: LCP, INP & CLS are part of Google Page Experience Signals. To improve your scores you need to improve your server speed, delay any unnecessary JavaScript, set dimensions on your images and embeds and compress your assets.

Usually large images, render blocking JavaScript, un-compressed code and slow hosting. To improve this you need to implement caching using a CDN, use WebP/AVIF images, delay JavaScript and optimise your database. All of this will be tested on real mobile networks.

technical-seo.html.q: How does Google crawl a website and how can I improve my crawl budget?
technical-seo.html.a: Googlebot will crawl your site using links and sitemaps. Google have allocated a crawl budget for your domain. You can improve your crawl budget by blocking any low value parameter URLs, fixing redirect chains and broken links, removing any soft 404s and keeping your XML sitemap clean.

technical-seo.html.q: What are the most common signs I need a technical audit?
technical-seo.html.a: Sudden traffic/impression drop, pages going out of index, slow mobile site speeds, increasing ‘Crawled - currently not indexed’ / ‘Discovered - currently not indexed’ in Search Console and a recent redesign/migration.

technical-seo.html.q: What is included in a technical SEO audit for ecommerce websites?
